sections.heading: First 10 minutes: safety and 911
paragraphs: A collision on Major highways and arterials in Ann Arbor or surface streets in Ann Arbor can escalate quickly. If vehicles are drivable and it is safe, move to a shoulder or parking lot. Turn on hazard lights.

Call 911 when anyone reports pain, airbags deploy, fluids leak, or traffic is blocked. Ann Arbor County / local jurisdiction dispatch will route Ann Arbor police or state patrol depending on location.
list: Stay inside the vehicle with seatbelts on if traffic passes closely at highway speed
Do not admit fault — describe facts only
Request a crash report number before officers leave

sections.heading: Ann Arbor documentation checklist
paragraphs: Photograph all vehicles, license plates, VIN stickers, skid marks, traffic signals, and visible injuries. Ann Arbor insurers expect timestamped photos.
Collect names and phone numbers from witnesses — independent accounts matter on Major highways and arterials in Ann Arbor and in Ann Arbor County / local jurisdiction.
Exchange insurance policy numbers and registration; note employer if the other driver was working.

sections.heading: Medical care within 24 hours
paragraphs: Ann Arbor has Ann Arbor area hospitals and emergency departments among its major facilities. Verify the nearest trauma center if injuries may be serious.
Whiplash, concussion, and internal injuries may appear hours later. A same-day urgent care or ER visit creates a medical record insurers cannot easily dismiss.

sections.heading: Michigan reporting rules
paragraphs: Michigan requires crash reporting when injuries, death, or significant property damage occur. Minimum liability limits are 50/100/10.
Cooperate with officers; request a copy of the report through the investigating agency. If police do not respond, check https://www.michigan.gov/mdot/ for self-report thresholds.

sections.heading: Insurance notification without hurting your claim
paragraphs: Notify your carrier with basic facts — date, location, vehicles involved. Decline recorded statements until you understand your coverage and injuries.
Michigan no-fault rules may limit lawsuits unless injuries exceed thresholds — verify with counsel.

sections.heading: Evidence preservation in Ann Arbor
paragraphs: Dashcam, Ring doorbell, and business security footage near High-traffic corridors in Ann Arbor, MI is often deleted within 7–30 days. Send written preservation letters when appropriate.
Save repair estimates, rental receipts, and mileage to medical appointments.

paragraphs: Consider a free consultation if you were hospitalized, fault is disputed, a commercial vehicle was involved, or the adjuster offers a quick settlement before treatment finishes.
